scenario: Peter is building a little 'team page' for the company website and asks about everyone, so the team describes each other with relative clauses (defining and non-defining, whose, where, and contact clauses with the pronoun left out). Kate: 'Den is the man whose mug you must never touch.' Alex: 'Pol is the guy who makes the famous smoothies.' Pol: 'Kate, who loves team-buildings, is our manager.' They also describe places: 'the café where we have lunch', 'the corner where the plant lives', 'the day when Alex was late.' Peter reads a contact clause back: 'The photo you sent is great.' Warm, funny, affectionate descriptions. Use clear relative clauses: defining (who/which/that/whose/where/when), one or two non-defining with commas, and a contact clause (dropped object pronoun). Short B1 sentences.
